newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf refiners edgy amid talk of NYMEX delivery.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf refiners edgy amid talk of NYMEX delivery.

text.p: Refiners along the U.S. Gulf Coast remained edgy on Thursday amid mounting talk of a possible delivery of foreign crude into NYMEX, traders said.
Traders speculated that ARCO would deliver Nigerian Bonny Light upon expiry of the May contract next Tuesday.
As owner of the oil installations at Cushing, ARCO is seen as being in a sound position to make such a delivery.
"(ARCO) has the cheapest incremental cost," one Gulf Coast refiner said.

Exchange for Physcials (EFPs) have been commanding a premium of around six to eight cents, and got as high as 12 cents late last week, as traders attempt to shift out of paper positions to avoid the uncertainty of receiving a crude other than West Texas Intermediate/Cushing upon expiry.
A Bonny Light delivery into NYMEX would require the buyer to pay a premium of 60 cents a barrel.
Foreign barrels are rarely delivered into NYMEX. ARCO was again the star player several months ago when an Oseberg delivery appeared imminent. That cargo was eventually sold, averting the exchange.
Elsewhere among foreign crudes, a European major was still seen offering Brent at WTI/Cushing minus $1.15 into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).
A trading house was flirting with the possibility of bringing in end-May Brent for WTI minus 85 cents delivered.
The June spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.45-55 a barrel Thursday afternoon, narrower than Wednesday but still high enough to encourage transatlantic trade.
In Latin America, a European major sold a Colombian Cusiana cargo loading May 21-22 fob Covenas for around WTI/Cushing minus $1.50-60 a barrel.
